result:
Understood. You've told me what you want; the one thing left is how it gets built, and that's a quick call. Here are the real options, built on what's already on the Pi:

**1. Add it to the taproom app (my pick).** Batch tracking becomes a new section of the Flask app you already run, with its own tables in the same SQLite database. Brewers use a tablet or phone at the brewhouse, and a cheap USB or Bluetooth barcode scanner types the sack's lot number into the form, so there's no typing with wet hands. Labels print from the same app.
*Trade-off:* there's one thing to run and back up. A bug in the new part could, in principle, disturb tabs during service.

**2. A separate small app on the same Pi.** It works the same way for the brewers, but it has its own app and database file, kept apart from tabs.
*Trade-off:* a problem in one can't touch the other. You'd have two things to start, update and back up.

I dropped off-the-shelf brewery software. It's a subscription and would sit apart from what you've already built, and you came here to build it.

I'd go with **1**, because one system on one Pi is less to look after. I'll keep the batch code in its own section so it doesn't tangle with tabs. Unless you'd rather have 2, I'll go with that.

This is a project-sized piece, so the design will be a written document. I'll save it as `specs/batch-tracking.md`. A reviewer will read it before I hand it to you, and I may come back once with a few questions only you can answer. The project folder isn't under version control yet, so I'll set that up to keep the spec in, unless you'd rather I didn't.
